title: Weather Alert: दिल्ली समेत इन 10 राज्यों में फिर बरसेंगे बादल, मॉनसून की विदाई के बीच IMD ने जारी किया बारिश का अलर्ट - Janbhawna Times
article_text:
Weather Alert: दिल्ली समेत इन 10 राज्यों में फिर बरसेंगे बादल, मॉनसून की विदाई के बीच IMD ने जारी किया बारिश का अलर्ट

मॉनसून की विदाई के बीच IMD ने दिल्ली समेत 10 राज्यों में आने वाले दिनों में बारिश की संभावना जताई है। 6 से 8 अक्टूबर के बीच कई इलाकों में मौसम बदल सकता है।

नई दिल्ली: देश के कई हिस्सों से दक्षिण-पश्चिम मॉनसून अब धीरे-धीरे विदा हो रहा है। इसी बीच मौसम विभाग ने आने वाले दिनों में कई राज्यों में बारिश की संभावना जताई है। भारत मौसम विज्ञान विभाग (IMD) के अनुसार पंजाब, हरियाणा, राजस्थान, जम्मू-कश्मीर, हिमाचल प्रदेश, उत्तराखंड, बिहार, झारखंड, छत्तीसगढ़ और महाराष्ट्र के कुछ हिस्सों से मॉनसून की वापसी के लिए परिस्थितियां अनुकूल बनी हुई हैं। हालांकि, इसके बावजूद कई राज्यों में बारिश का दौर देखने को मिल सकता है।

भारतीय समाचार

ज़्यादा जानें खेल समाचार सूर्य गोचर प्रभाव धर्म समाचार

दिल्ली समेत इन राज्यों में बारिश का अलर्ट

IMD के पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक 6 से 8 अक्टूबर के बीच पंजाब, हरियाणा, चंडीगढ़ और दिल्ली के अलावा पश्चिमी और पूर्वी उत्तर प्रदेश में कुछ जगहों पर बारिश हो सकती है। पहाड़ी राज्यों जम्मू-कश्मीर, हिमाचल प्रदेश और उत्तराखंड में भी मौसम बदलने की संभावना है। इन इलाकों में कुछ स्थानों पर बारिश का अलर्ट जारी किया गया है।

मध्य प्रदेश और छत्तीसगढ़ के कुछ हिस्सों में भी बारिश हो सकती है। इसके अलावा बिहार, झारखंड और अरुणाचल प्रदेश में बारिश की संभावना को देखते हुए मौसम विभाग ने लोगों को सतर्क रहने की सलाह दी है।

दिल्ली में फिलहाल मौसम रहेगा साफ

दिल्ली-एनसीआर में शनिवार, 3 अक्टूबर को आसमान मुख्य रूप से साफ रहने का अनुमान है। राजधानी में दिन के समय तापमान 33 से 35 डिग्री सेल्सियस के आसपास रह सकता है, जबकि न्यूनतम तापमान 22 से 24 डिग्री के बीच रहने की संभावना है। फिलहाल दिल्ली में तापमान सामान्य के करीब रहने का अनुमान है। रविवार यानी 4 अक्टूबर को भी दिल्ली में मौसम साफ रहने की उम्मीद है। इस दिन अधिकतम तापमान 34 से 36 डिग्री और न्यूनतम तापमान 23 से 25 डिग्री सेल्सियस के बीच रह सकता है।

बौद्ध धर्म

मौसम विभाग के अनुसार दक्षिण भारत, पूर्वोत्तर और पूर्वी भारत के कई हिस्सों में बारिश का दौर जारी रह सकता है। कुछ इलाकों में भारी से बहुत भारी बारिश होने की भी संभावना है। ऐसे में मॉनसून की विदाई के बीच देश के अलग-अलग हिस्सों में मौसम का मिजाज बदलता नजर आएगा।

title: Kerala Rain Update: Is School Holiday on July 2? IMD Issues Orange Alert; District-Wise Weather Forecast - Goodreturns
article_text:
Kerala is set to witness another intense spell of monsoon rainfall over the coming days, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecasting widespread rain across the state until July 5. The latest weather update has prompted heightened vigilance, particularly in northern Kerala, where heavy to very heavy rainfall is expected to disrupt normal life.
As the southwest monsoon regains strength, several districts are likely to experience persistent showers, thunderstorms and gusty winds. The weather department has urged residents to remain alert as heavy rainfall could trigger flooding, waterlogging and landslides in vulnerable areas.
The active monsoon conditions are expected to affect road connectivity, tourism, plantation activities, local businesses and fishing operations. Residents living in flood-prone or landslide-prone regions have been advised to closely follow updates issued by district administrations and disaster management authorities.
According to the latest IMD forecast, rainfall activity is expected to continue across several districts through the first week of July, with Yellow Alerts remaining in force across multiple regions.
The IMD has issued a Yellow Alert for Kozhikode, Kannur and Kasaragod, where isolated heavy rainfall is likely during the day.
On July 3, a Yellow Alert will remain in effect for Idukki, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Kannur and Kasaragod, with heavy rain expected at isolated places across these districts.
The Yellow Alert will be extended to Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Kannur and Kasaragod on July 4, as the active monsoon conditions continue over large parts of the state.
For July 5, the IMD has placed Kozhikode, Kannur and Kasaragod under a Yellow Alert, indicating the possibility of isolated heavy rainfall in these northern Kerala districts.
The IMD has noted that rainfall forecasts and alert levels may change depending on evolving weather systems. Residents are therefore advised to keep track of the latest district-wise bulletins issued by the weather department.
As of now, there is no state-wide school holiday in Kerala for Wednesday, July 2.
School closures in Kerala are generally announced district-wise by the respective District Collectors based on local weather conditions, rainfall intensity, flooding and other safety concerns. Since heavy rain is expected in several districts, parents, students and school authorities are advised to monitor official announcements issued by the concerned district administrations.
If rainfall intensifies overnight or local conditions deteriorate, district officials may announce holidays for educational institutions in affected areas.

title: Meghalaya Records 60% Rainfall Deficit During Monsoon: IMD - Northeast Today
article_text:
NET Web Desk

Shillong, Oct 2: Meghalaya experienced a severe monsoon shortfall this year, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) reporting a 60 per cent rainfall deficit during the June–September southwest monsoon season. The state received only 1,077.1 mm of rain compared to the normal average of 2,695.3 mm.

Explore History

Even Sohra and Mawsynram, globally recognized for their exceptionally high rainfall, recorded deficits of 36 per cent and 34 per cent, respectively. The unusual decline in precipitation has heightened concerns over water availability across the state.

Officials noted that the Public Health Engineering (PHE) department has intensified efforts to ensure source sustainability and strengthen reliable drinking water supply systems, as the deficit poses challenges for communities dependent on consistent rainfall.

title: IMD forecasts heavy rain in Interior Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Keralam and northeastern states today - News On AIR
article_text:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Interior Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe and Tamil Nadu and some parts of North-Eastern states today.

IMD has also forecast thunderstorms with lightning and gusty winds over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Puducherry, Odisha and Madhya Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura today.

For Delhi, the weather department predicted a clear-sky day today with a maximum temperature of around 32 to 34 degrees Celsius and a minimum temperature to remain around 20 to 22 degrees Celsius.

title: Bihar Flood Relief गंडक की बाढ़ ने छीना सब कुछ, फिर किन्नर समाज ने ऐसे थामी बेघर हुए लोगों की जिंदगी! - Deshaj Times
article_text:
- Advertisement -

Bihar Flood Relief: पश्चिम चंपारण के नौतन प्रखंड में गंडक नदी का कहर जारी है। बाढ़ के कारण हजारों परिवार बेघर हो गए हैं और सुरक्षित ठिकानों की तलाश में बांधों व तटबंधों पर शरण लेने को मजबूर हैं। इसी मुश्किल घड़ी में पश्चिम चंपारण के बाढ़ पीड़ितों के लिए किन्नर समाज देवदूत बनकर सामने आया है।

- Advertisement - ज़्यादा जानें अखबार पढ़ें प्रचार करें बौद्ध पुस्तकें पढ़ें

बनकटवा और मंगलपुर बांध पर अपना सब कुछ छोड़कर रह रहे परिवारों के बीच खुशी किन्नर, कृष्णा किन्नर और पंडिताइन किन्नर ने राहत सामग्री का वितरण किया। उन्होंने बाढ़ से प्रभावित लोगों की समस्याओं को भी सुना और उनकी जरूरतों को समझा। किन्नर समाज से मिली इस मदद से अस्थायी ठिकानों पर रह रहे परिवारों को तत्काल राहत मिली है, जब Bihar Flood Relief की सख्त दरकार है।

- Advertisement -

गंडक के पानी में डूबे घर, खुले आसमान के नीचे जिंदगी

नौतन प्रखंड के कई इलाकों में गंडक नदी का पानी घरों में घुस गया है, जिससे लोगों की दिनचर्या बुरी तरह प्रभावित हुई है। अपना सामान समेटकर सुरक्षित स्थानों पर पहुंचे लोग अब बांधों पर तंबू लगाकर या खुले आसमान के नीचे जीवन गुजारने को मजबूर हैं। बनकटवा और मंगलपुर बांध पर बड़ी संख्या में ऐसे ही प्रभावित परिवारों ने आश्रय लिया है। इन लोगों के सामने भोजन, पीने का पानी और रोजमर्रा की जरूरतों की भीषण परेशानी खड़ी हो गई है। सामान्य गतिविधियां पूरी तरह से ठप हैं।

- Advertisement -

किन्नर समाज की मानवीय पहल: बांटी जरूरी सामग्री

संकट की इस घड़ी में खुशी किन्नर, कृष्णा किन्नर और पंडिताइन किन्नर राहत सामग्री लेकर बाढ़ पीड़ितों के बीच पहुंचीं। उन्होंने एक-एक परिवार से बात की, उनकी तकलीफें जानीं और उनकी बुनियादी जरूरतों के बारे में जानकारी ली। इसके बाद, उन्होंने अपनी क्षमता के अनुसार उपलब्ध जरूरी सामानों का वितरण किया। इस मानवीय पहल के दौरान राहत पाने वाले परिवारों ने किन्नर समाज का आभार व्यक्त किया।

‘आपदा के समय जरूरतमंद की सहायता सबसे जरूरी है। संकट की स्थिति में लोगों की पहचान से ज्यादा उनकी जरूरत मायने रखती है।’

राहत वितरण करने पहुंचीं खुशी किन्नर ने कहा कि आपदा के समय जरूरतमंद की सहायता सबसे महत्वपूर्ण होती है। उन्होंने जोर देकर कहा कि संकट की स्थिति में किसी व्यक्ति की पहचान से कहीं अधिक उसकी जरूरत मायने रखती है। किन्नर समाज ने यह भी आश्वासन दिया कि वे अपनी क्षमता के अनुसार बाढ़ प्रभावित परिवारों की मदद जारी रखेंगे। प्रभावित लोगों का कहना है कि ऐसे मुश्किल समय में जरूरी सामान मिलने से उनकी तत्काल आवश्यकताओं को पूरा करने में बहुत मदद मिलती है। यह एकजुटता और मानवीयता का संदेश है जो संकटकाल में उम्मीद जगाता है।

Bihar Floods 2026, Over 50 Lakh People Affected Across 15 Districts

Bihar Floods 2026 worsen as the Ganga crosses its previous highest flood level at Patna’s Gandhi Ghat, affecting 50 lakh people across 15 districts and triggering alerts.

By Anshu Shukla - Oct 3, 2026, 12:40 IST

Share
Table of Contents
☰

Bihar Floods 2026 situation has intensified, with around 50 lakh people affected across 15 districts of the state. The crisis has worsened after the Ganga crossed its previous Highest Flood Level (HFL) at Gandhi Ghat in Patna, prompting authorities to issue alerts for downstream areas.

North Western Bihar Floods 2026

Recently, the Champaran Floods 2026 have worsened after continuous rainfall in Nepal’s Gandak basin and North Bihar. As of 3rd October, the Gandak River reached a record 91.25 metres in Bagaha, while embankments breached at several places. Over 200 villages across Bihar have been affected, with relief and rescue operations continuing in flood-hit areas.

Major Causes of Floods in Bihar

Floods in Bihar are caused by a combination of natural factors, geographical conditions and human activities.

Heavy Monsoon Rainfall: Intense and prolonged monsoon rainfall increases the volume of water flowing into Bihar’s rivers and can quickly push them beyond their carrying capacity.
River Overflow: Rivers such as the Ganga, Kosi, Gandak and Bagmati frequently experience rising water levels during the monsoon, resulting in inundation of nearby areas.
Siltation of Riverbeds: Large quantities of sediment and silt carried by Himalayan rivers gradually raise riverbeds and reduce their water-carrying capacity.
Flat and Low-Lying Terrain: Much of Bihar consists of flat alluvial plains, allowing floodwaters to spread over large areas and drain slowly.
Embankment-Related Problems: Embankments protect settlements and agricultural land but can also restrict natural drainage. Breaches, poor maintenance and waterlogging can worsen flood impacts.
Deforestation and Land-Use Changes: Loss of vegetation in catchment areas can increase surface runoff and soil erosion, adding more sediment to rivers.
Urbanisation: Unplanned urban growth and the conversion of natural drainage channels can reduce the ability of cities and towns to absorb and drain excess water.
‹
›
Why is Bihar Highly Vulnerable to Floods?

Bihar is among India’s most flood-prone states because of its geography, river system and socio-economic conditions. A large part of the state consists of fertile but low-lying alluvial plains, while many rivers entering Bihar originate in the Himalayan region.

Key factors behind Bihar’s vulnerability include:

Himalayan rivers: Rivers originating in the Himalayas carry substantial amounts of water and sediment into Bihar during the monsoon.
Low-gradient plains: The state’s relatively flat terrain slows the movement of floodwaters.
High population density: Large populations live in flood-prone areas, increasing the number of people exposed to disasters.
Agricultural dependence: A significant rural population depends on agriculture, making floods a major threat to livelihoods and food security.
Drainage constraints: Water can remain stagnant for long periods because of inadequate natural and artificial drainage.
Transboundary river systems: Several major rivers enter Bihar from Nepal, making effective flood management dependent partly on upstream conditions and cooperation.
Major Rivers Responsible for Floods in Bihar

Bihar’s flood vulnerability is closely linked to its major Himalayan and Gangetic rivers, which carry high volumes of water and sediment during the monsoon.

Ganga: The principal river of Bihar; rising water levels can inundate large areas along its floodplain.
Kosi: Known for its high sediment load and shifting course, making it one of Bihar’s most flood-prone rivers.
Gandak: Originating in the Himalayas, it causes flooding in parts of north-western Bihar during heavy rainfall.
Bagmati: Frequently causes floods in north Bihar, particularly during intense monsoon rainfall.
Burhi Gandak: Its overflowing waters affect several districts of north and central Bihar.
Kamla-Balan: A Himalayan river that contributes to flooding in parts of Madhubani, Darbhanga and adjoining areas.
Ghaghra: Its high water levels can affect areas near its confluence with the Ganga.
Punpun: A significant cause of flooding in parts of south Bihar, including Patna region.
Impact of Bihar Floods 2026

Northwestern Bihar Floods 2026 have created significant humanitarian, economic and infrastructural challenges.

Human displacement: Flooding forces vulnerable families to move to safer locations and relief camps.
Agricultural losses: Floodwaters can damage standing crops, farmland and livestock, affecting rural incomes.
Infrastructure damage: Roads, bridges, houses, schools and other public infrastructure may be damaged or disrupted.
Transport disruption: Flooding can affect road and rail connectivity, making movement difficult.
Health risks: Contaminated water and stagnant water can increase the risk of waterborne diseases and other health problems.
Livelihood disruption: Small businesses, agricultural workers and rural households may lose income during prolonged flooding.
Food and water insecurity: Disruption of supplies can create shortages of safe drinking water, food and essential medicines.
Pressure on administration: Large-scale flooding requires extensive deployment of NDRF, SDRF, boats, relief camps and community kitchens.
Government Measures for Flood Management in Bihar

Bihar government follows a multi-dimensional approach to flood management, combining embankment protection, drainage, flood forecasting, rescue operations, relief and disaster preparedness. The Water Resources Department is responsible for flood-control works, including embankments, river-bank protection and drainage of waterlogged areas.

Embankment Construction and Maintenance: The government undertakes the construction, strengthening and maintenance of embankments to protect flood-prone settlements and agricultural areas.
Anti-Erosion Measures: Revetments, land spurs and other river-bank protection works are undertaken at vulnerable locations to reduce erosion and protect embankments.
Flood Forecasting and Monitoring: River water levels and vulnerable locations are monitored to support timely warnings and preparedness.
Flood Control Orders: The Water Resources Department issues annual flood-control guidelines and operational directions for managing vulnerable rivers and embankments; a specific Flood Control Order 2026 is also listed by the department.
Flood Protection Forces: Special flood-fighting teams are constituted to provide technical assistance for protecting embankments and other vulnerable sites during the flood season.
NDRF and SDRF Deployment: Disaster-response forces are deployed for rescue, evacuation and emergency relief in severely affected areas.
Relief and Rehabilitation: The Disaster Management Department coordinates response, relief, rehabilitation and reconstruction, with a focus on vulnerable communities.
Flood and Drainage Schemes: The state implements flood-protection and drainage schemes to reduce inundation and waterlogging in vulnerable areas.
Community-Based Preparedness: Bihar’s flood-disaster management framework includes pre-flood preparation, relief and rescue during floods, post-flood action and reconstruction, helping strengthen disaster preparedness at different stages.
Challenges in Flood Management in Bihar

Bihar faces persistent challenges in managing floods due to its geographical vulnerability, heavy sedimentation, inadequate drainage, infrastructure limitations and recurring monsoon floods. These challenges are further complicated by the transboundary nature of several major rivers.

High Sediment Load: Himalayan rivers carry large amounts of silt, reducing the carrying capacity of river channels and raising riverbeds.
Embankment Breaches: Weak or damaged embankments can lead to sudden flooding, while their maintenance requires continuous monitoring and investment.
Poor Drainage: Inadequate drainage and blocked natural channels can result in prolonged waterlogging even after river levels decline.
Transboundary Rivers: Several major rivers originate in Nepal, making effective flood management dependent on timely data sharing and cooperation between India and Nepal.
Changing Rainfall Patterns: Climate change and extreme rainfall events can increase uncertainty in flood forecasting and preparedness.
High Population Exposure: A large population lives in low-lying and flood-prone areas, making evacuation, relief and rehabilitation difficult.
Agricultural Dependence: Frequent floods cause crop and livestock losses, affecting the livelihoods of rural communities.
Limited Floodplain Management: Encroachment and unplanned development in flood-prone areas can obstruct natural drainage and increase flood risks.
